newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rennes plans airfreight conference for October 17.
newsitem.headline: Rennes plans airfreight conference for October 17.

text.p: Rennes-St Jacques airport in Brittany, is organising a one-day conference on October 17 to promote as Rennes a regional airfreight centre, a Chamber of Commerce official told Reuters.

"We contacted firms in the region and in particular, those in the automotive, computers and pharmaceuticals sectors, to seek their views on the kind of conference agenda they would like to see," he said.
The Chamber of Commerce is responsible for the airport's management.
The conference themes include air transport's place in the logistics chain with a case study on its efficiency in handling special shipments of automotive parts.

The speakers on covering this subject will be Denis Chevalier, a consultant commissioned by the United Nations to undertake a mission on logistics and Michel Bigot, director of Gefco Special, a branch of French forwarding group, Gefco, itself part of the PSA Peugeot Citroen automobile group, the official said.
Information techology in the sector will also be discussed in a a paper presented by the French manager of air cargo information service, Traxon Europe, Guy Deschamps.
Air France Cargo's regional manager for western France, Eric Marro, will be present at the conference.
Other airlines, among them Deutsche Lufthansa AG and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, as well as forwarding groups, have been invited, the official added.
Rennes handled 2,126 tonnes of air cargo and trucked airfreight in the first eight months of 1996, an increase of 28.5 percent on 1995 levels, airport authority figures showed.
The airport's sole "all cargo" flight is a nightly service operated by Air Jet, the airline subsidiary of French air and road express distribution group, Jet Services.

French airline, L'Aeropostale, carries overnight mail between its Paris-Charles de Gaulle hub and Rennes on a regular basis using Boeing 737QC aircraft. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
